question: What are the three core pillars of a comprehensive school health programme?

options.A: Health instruction, health services, and healthy school environment
options.B: Nutritional feeding, physical education, and disease screening
options.C: First aid administration, psychological counseling, and water supply
options.D: Teacher training, community outreach, and sanitation control

explanation: The standard triad comprising any recognized school health framework consists of education, direct health intervention services, and maintaining a safe physical and psychosocial environment. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why is the active involvement of school management critical to the success of a School Health Programme?

options.A: Administrators are solely responsible for diagnosing student illnesses on site
options.B: Teachers refuse to conduct classes unless health officers are present
options.C: Government funding is exclusively distributed through private school principals
options.D: Management translates broad health policies into practical institutional operations

explanation: Without administrative backing, national or regional health guidelines remain theoretical documents rather than active protective measures for students. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is the primary responsibility of school management regarding national health policies?

options.A: Reporting non-compliant parents directly to law enforcement agencies
options.B: Exempting teachers from complying with mandatory vaccination protocols
options.C: Rewriting federal legislation to match private school financial interests
options.D: Domesticating and operationalizing them within the specific school environment

explanation: Administrators must take broad government mandates and adapt them into actionable, site-specific rules and daily routines for their particular student population. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h2)

question: Which health protocol is most essential for a school management team to establish locally?

options.A: Clear accident response and communicable disease containment procedures
options.B: Strict dietary restrictions prohibiting home-prepared food items
options.C: Daily physical fitness grading recorded by administrative staff
options.D: Mandatory genetic counseling for all incoming adolescent students

explanation: Localized protocols must address immediate safety threats such as injuries on the playground or sudden outbreaks of infectious ailments like cholera or measles. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h2)

question: Which infrastructural feature is most critical for preventing waterborne disease outbreaks in a school?

options.B: Paved parking lots for staff and visitor vehicles
options.C: Tiled flooring throughout all academic hallways
options.D: Reliable access to a clean portable water supply

explanation: Safe drinking water is the primary defense against waterborne illnesses such as typhoid and gastroenteritis in school-aged children. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h3)

question: A school administrator notices frequent student absenteeism due to diarrheal illnesses during the rainy season. What is the most appropriate infrastructural intervention?

options.A: Issuing warning letters to food vendors operating outside the school gates
options.B: Purchasing modern computers to improve computer-based health instruction
options.C: Upgrading and securing the primary water source and functional handwashing stations
options.D: Extending the daily teaching hours to compensate for missed academic lessons

explanation: Addressing waterborne illnesses requires direct intervention in water safety and personal hygiene infrastructure within the school premises. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h3)

question: What does dedicated budgeting for a school health programme primarily ensure?

options.A: Complete elimination of all tuition fees for indigent students
options.B: Consistent availability of first aid supplies, screening tools, and sanitation materials
options.C: Immediate construction of Olympic-sized sports facilities
options.D: Guaranteed annual salary bonuses for visiting public health nurses

explanation: A designated budget prevents stockouts of basic medical consumables and ensures routine sanitation maintenance is never delayed. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why is prioritizing preventive health spending advantageous for school administrators?

options.A: It eliminates the need to employ qualified school health teachers
options.B: It completely transfers medical liability onto the parents
options.C: It averts major health crises and reduces expensive reactive treatments later
options.D: It guarantees an increase in federal grants for academic performance

explanation: Investing in simple preventive measures like handwashing soap and regular checkups costs far less than managing a full-scale disease outbreak or severe injury emergency. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h4)

question: What is a key administrative duty in supporting school health instruction?

options.A: Grading national board examinations for health science students
options.B: Selecting students exempt from learning basic hygiene principles
options.C: Personally teaching all biology and physical education classes
options.D: Allocating dedicated timetable periods and providing instructional materials

explanation: Management must protect instructional time for health topics and ensure teachers have access to proper curricula and textbooks. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h5)

question: How does integrating health education into the daily curriculum benefit students beyond the classroom?

options.A: It guarantees that children will never contract infectious diseases
options.B: It prepares every student for an immediate career in professional nursing
options.C: It instills lifelong disease prevention habits and personal hygiene practices
options.D: It replaces the need for physical health infrastructure like clinics

explanation: Classroom instruction translates into real-world behavioral changes, empowering students to make healthier lifestyle choices throughout their lives. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h5)

question: Which group serves as the primary community partner for executing school immunization and screening exercises?

options.A: Commercial transport unions operating near the school gates
options.B: Private real estate developers constructing nearby residential estates
options.C: National security agencies and military personnel
options.D: Local primary health care centers and public health nurses

explanation: Primary health care facilities provide the clinical expertise and personnel needed to conduct routine checkups and vaccinations on school grounds. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is the primary advantage of building strong relationships between school management and the Parent-Teacher Association?

options.A: Transferring the financial burden of teacher salaries onto families
options.B: Allowing parents to directly dictate daily classroom teaching schedules
options.C: Enforcing strict disciplinary measures without administrative oversight
options.D: Mobilizing community resources and cooperative support for health initiatives

explanation: Parent-Teacher Associations often provide vital grassroots backing, funding, and volunteer labor to improve school health facilities and programs. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of monitoring and evaluation within a school health programme?

options.A: Complying with secret security directives from federal agencies
options.B: Calculating the exact profit margins generated by school canteens
options.C: Assessing program effectiveness and identifying areas needing quality improvement
options.D: Punishing staff members who report student health incidents

explanation: Regular evaluations allow administrators to see what is working, catch emerging safety hazards, and refine health interventions accordingly. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h7)

question: Which administrative record is most useful when evaluating the impact of school health interventions over an academic year?

options.A: Comprehensive financial audit reports of textbook purchases
options.B: Teacher attendance registers and staff meeting minutes
options.C: Extracurricular sports competition trophies and participation lists
options.D: Student health clinic logs and illness-related absenteeism records

explanation: Tracking clinic visits and missed school days provides concrete data on the health status of the student body and the success of preventive measures. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h7)
